section_summary: This closing section consists chiefly of Federal Communications Commission cover letters and monitored Morse transmissions from Jakarta Radio station PMC, repeatedly announcing an “American Hour” of news and revelations for listeners in the United States. It also contains a lengthy American Embassy report translating more than two hundred intercepted Japanese commercial, shipping, personnel, diplomatic-welfare, and private messages exchanged across East and Southeast Asia, together with a State Department forwarding note. A separate broadcast-intelligence report summarizes Japanese commentary on the anticipated battle for the Philippines, José P. Laurel’s opposition to Filipino conscription, and Akiyoshi Tajiri’s explanation of Philippine martial law.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC warning transmission to the United States
subfiles.about: A monitored Morse transmission announces Jakarta Radio's American program and urges United States listeners to receive its forthcoming news.
subfiles.summary: Jakarta Radio PMC, Djakarta, Djawa, 18,135 kilocycles: its American Hour promises news and revelations Americans supposedly cannot get elsewhere.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC forwards additional intercepts of Jakarta Radio in response to Berle's request.
subfiles.summary: FCC's G. E. Sterling sends further confidential Jakarta Radio intercepts with a list of enclosures.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: An FCC monitoring station records PMC's standard appeal to American listeners.
subfiles.summary: PMC American Hour intercept: 18,135 kilocycles, program at 1800 Pacific War Time promising important news; severe fading but good keying.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC intercept of 23 August 1944
subfiles.about: The monitored transmission repeats Jakarta Radio's promotional warning for its American program.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept of August 23, 1944 calling the US and promising vital news; heavy static, poor keying, blind transmission to KAIA.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC intercept of 25 August 1944
subfiles.about: PMC broadcasts its recurring announcement of an American Hour from Jakarta.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept of August 25, 1944 promising an hour of news at 1800 Pacific War Time and another transmission at 1135 Tokyo time; light static.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC sends Berle another group of Jakarta Radio intercepts.
subfiles.summary: FCC registered letter answers Berle's standing request for Jakarta Radio intercepts, signed by Sterling.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: A monitored transmission urges Americans to listen to Jakarta Radio's promised international-affairs revelations.
subfiles.summary: PMC American Hour intercept giving wavelength, 1800 Pacific War Time program and another transmission at 1135 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: The intercept records PMC's recurring invitation to the United States audience.
subfiles.summary: Hand-sent PMC intercept identifies Jakarta Radio on 18,135 kilocycles, promises vital news, and schedules the next call for 1135 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: Incomplete Jakarta Radio PMC intercept
subfiles.about: An interrupted transmission begins PMC's standard American Hour announcement but goes off the air during the text.
subfiles.summary: Incomplete PMC intercept that begins identifying Jakarta and its purpose, then goes off before finishing.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: The complete monitored warning promotes Jakarta Radio's broadcasts to America.
subfiles.summary: PMC American Hour intercept: 18,135 kilocycles, program at 1800 Pacific War Time, news unavailable elsewhere, returning next day.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling forwards another set of Jakarta Radio intercepts to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: FCC confidential letter sends intercepts at Berle's request, signed by Sterling.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC intercept of 7 September 1944
subfiles.about: PMC delivers its standard American Hour promotion and announces a subsequent Tokyo-time transmission.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept of September 7, 1944: important news and revelations, 18,135 kilocycles, next transmission at 1135 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC intercept of 8 September 1944
subfiles.about: An FCC monitor records a fading, partially garbled version of PMC's standard appeal.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept of September 8, 1944 with missing words promising vital news and another transmission around 1130 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: PMC repeats its regular announcement for the American program over a poorly sent signal.
subfiles.summary: PMC American Hour intercept: program at 1800 Pacific War Time with international news and revelations; next broadcast 1135 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC forwards additional Jakarta Radio monitoring material.
subfiles.summary: FCC registered confidential letter sends enclosures at Berle's request, with the State wireless-broadcasting file reference.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: The monitored message advertises Jakarta Radio's American broadcast and its purported exclusive news.
subfiles.summary: PMC American Hour intercept: 18,135 kilocycles, 1800 Pacific War Time, vital revelations, next transmission 1135 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling sends Berle further FCC intercepts of Jakarta Radio.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: PMC's promotional transmission is monitored with static but no interference.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept with keying corrections promising news unavailable elsewhere and another transmission about 1130 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: A poorly hand-sent PMC transmission repeats the station's warning to American listeners.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept promising important news, asking Americans to prepare for the wireless-telephone broadcast, with another transmission about 1130.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC provides another confidential Jakarta Radio intercept enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Sterling sends an enclosed intercept at Berle's request, filed under the wireless-broadcasting designation.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: The intercept records PMC's familiar appeal to American audiences.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept: 18,135 kilocycles, 1800 Pacific War Time program, news and revelations, next call 1130 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: Voluntary Report No. 107 on intercepted Japanese messages
subfiles.about: The embassy introduces translations of Japanese commercial and miscellaneous messages intercepted between 1 August and 2 September 1944.
subfiles.summary: Embassy Voluntary Report 107: traffic intercepted by an Allied monitoring unit and translated by the American-operated Translation Center, mostly commercial; texts on Japanese coercive-service recruitment omitted.

subfiles.title: Translations of intercepted Japanese commercial and miscellaneous messages
subfiles.about: The enclosure translates more than two hundred intercepted messages exchanged among Japanese-controlled commercial, transport, banking, government, and private correspondents.
subfiles.summary: The messages range across Bangkok, Saigon, Shanghai, Tokyo, Hanoi, Canton, and other Asian centers and concern rice, pepper, beans, rubber, shipping, warehouses, insurance, remittances, staffing, and wartime shortages. Several report Thailand's 1944 cabinet and regency changes, while others carry Red Cross inquiries, internee news, death notifications, and family greetings. The compilation also reveals extensive coordination among Japanese trading houses, banks, transport associations, military authorities, and local branches under increasingly difficult wartime conditions. Many translations preserve the original cable numbers, languages, prices, quantities, and routing information.

subfiles.title: State Department transmittal of Voluntary Report No. 107
subfiles.about: The Secretary of State sends the Director of Censorship a copy of the Chungking embassy's report on intercepted Japanese commercial messages.
subfiles.summary: Confidential note sends Voluntary Report 107 of October 5, 1944 for censorship authorities.

subfiles.title: Foreign Broadcast Intelligence daily report for 4 October 1944
subfiles.about: The report summarizes Japanese and Philippine broadcasts about naval strategy, Filipino conscription, and martial law.
subfiles.summary: FBIS report of October 4, 1944: Admiral Suetsugu says air battles will decide the war and the Philippines are decisive; Laurel again rejects compulsory Filipino combat service; Tajiri calls martial law a Filipino-created mechanism.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling forwards additional monitored Jakarta Radio transmissions.
subfiles.summary: FCC registered confidential letter sends further Jakarta intercepts to Berle, signed by Sterling.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: A well-keyed PMC transmission promotes Jakarta Radio's American Hour.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept promising news unavailable elsewhere at 1800 Pacific War Time on 18,135 kilocycles, next transmission 1130.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: PMC repeats its standard American-service announcement through moderate static and interference.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept identifying Jakarta, Java and 18,135 kilocycles, promising exclusive news; further transmission at 1130.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC sends another installment of Jakarta Radio intercepts to Berle.
subfiles.summary: FCC confidential letter furnishing monitoring material at Berle's request, signed by Sterling.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC intercept of 5 October 1944
subfiles.about: PMC's American Hour announcement is copied despite heavy atmospheric noise.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept of October 5, 1944 promising important news unavailable elsewhere, ending with 1130 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling forwards further Jakarta Radio intercepts under the 12 October file reference.
subfiles.summary: FCC confidential registered letter continues the regular transmittals of Jakarta Radio intercepts.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC intercept of 7 October 1944
subfiles.about: A poorly sent PMC transmission announces the American program and its claimed international revelations.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept of October 7, 1944 with operator corrections: Jakarta identity, frequency, 1800 Pacific War Time, next time 1130.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC transmits another set of Jakarta Radio monitoring records.
subfiles.summary: FCC cover letter to Berle signed by Sterling, supplying intercepts at Berle's request.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: PMC broadcasts the standard American Hour warning through severe atmospheric noise.
subfiles.summary: PMC American Hour intercept: Jakarta Radio, 18,135 kilocycles, 1800 start, revelations, next transmission 1130 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC American Hour intercept
subfiles.about: A second monitoring sheet records PMC's recurring promotional message.
subfiles.summary: Good hand-keyed PMC transmission promising vital news to the US and closing with notice of a later transmission.

subfiles.title: FCC letter transmitting further Jakarta Radio intercepts
subfiles.from: G. E. Sterling, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Adolph A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Sterling sends Berle the final group of Jakarta Radio intercepts in this file section.
subfiles.summary: FCC registered letter of October 17 supplying intercepts under Berle's request, filed by State October 23.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC intercept of 14 October 1944
subfiles.about: PMC repeats its American Hour announcement after an initially unreadable mixture of code and music.
subfiles.summary: PMC intercept of October 14, 1944 promising an hour of news at 1800 Pacific War Time and referencing 1130 Tokyo time.

subfiles.title: Jakarta Radio PMC intercept, final sheet
subfiles.about: The file ends with another monitored version of PMC's appeal to American listeners.
subfiles.summary: Final PMC sheet with a garbled frequency, promising revelations and telling Americans to prepare for the broadcast; ends before the usual closing.
